01_long_tailed_weasel.visual_traits: unstriped cinnamon-brown coat, dark brown dorsal surface, pale cream-white underparts, dark brown tail with black tip, dark brown paws with light claws, furred tan muzzle with dark nose, small dark ears, slender body, long tail, visible whiskers, dark brown legs
01_long_tailed_weasel.wiki_clauses: The dorsal fur is brown in summer, while the underparts are whitish and tinged with yellowish or buffy brown from the chin to the inguinal region. | In northern areas in winter, the long-tailed weasel's fur becomes white, sometimes with yellow tints, but the tail retains its black tip.

02_hoary_marmot.visual_traits: silver-gray fur shoulders, unstriped drab-brown coat, dark brown fur head, white muzzle patch, white chin fur, dark brown paws, small dark nose, grizzled brown back, short bushy tail, visible whiskers, rounded ears
02_hoary_marmot.wiki_clauses: The head is black on the upper surface, with a white patch on the muzzle, white fur on the chin and around the lips, and grizzled black or brown fur elsewhere. | The word "hoary" refers to the silver-gray fur on their shoulders and upper back; the remainder of the upper parts have drab- or reddish-brown fur.

03_steller_sea_lion.visual_traits: unstriped tawny-brown coat, dark brown muzzle, dark brown flippers, short dark whiskers, smooth forehead, rounded ears, dark brown paws with visible claws, lighter tan belly, sleek head, robust body
03_steller_sea_lion.wiki_clauses: Adult animals are lighter in color than most sea lions, ranging from pale yellow to tawny and occasionally reddish. | Steller sea lion pups are born almost black, weighing around 23 kg , and remain dark in coloration for several months.

04_eastern_bluebird.visual_traits: bright blue head, back, and wings, rusty-orange breast, pale cream belly, blue tail, dark legs and feet, small black beak, smooth blue crown, dark eye, reddish-brown perch under feet
04_eastern_bluebird.wiki_clauses: Females are lighter with gray on the head and back and some blue on their wings and tail. | Male bluebirds have a bright head, back, and wings.

05_killdeer.eye_color_in_photo: dark reddish-brown eye with black pupil
05_killdeer.visual_traits: black breast bands, white shoulder stripe, brown upperparts, rufous fringes, white head patches, black head crown, pale cream underparts, brown legs, dark beak, barred tail feathers, brown wings, white tail band, pale cream belly, dark brown eye
05_killdeer.wiki_clauses: Its upperparts are mostly brown with rufous fringes, the head has patches of white and black, and two black bands cross the breast. | The latter also has a black subterminal band, a white terminal band, and barred white feathers on the outer portion of the tail.

06_red_shouldered_hawk.eye_color_in_photo: dark reddish-brown eye with black pupil
06_red_shouldered_hawk.visual_traits: reddish-brown shoulder patch, dark brown upperparts, pale spotted wings, reddish barred belly, pale cream underwing coverts, dark brown tail, long yellow legs, pale cream throat, dark beak, reddish-brown head, dark brown eye, pale buff breast, dark mottled feet
06_red_shouldered_hawk.wiki_clauses: Adults have brownish heads, reddish chests, and pale bellies with reddish bars. | These hawks' upper parts are dark with pale spots and they have long yellow legs.

07_common_five_lined_skink.visual_traits: five pale cream stripes, body; bright blue tail, body; dark brown scales, head; silver sheen, back; dark brown legs, limbs; pale cream belly, underside; small dark claws, feet; smooth scales, body
07_common_five_lined_skink.wiki_clauses: Young American five-lined skinks are dark brown to black with five distinctive white to yellowish stripes running along the body and a bright blue tail. | The blue color fades to light blue with age, and the stripes also may slowly disappear.

08_western_ribbon_snake.visual_traits: three longitudinal pale cream stripes, dark olive-brown dorsal scales, unmarked whitish upper labials, blackish-brown head, smooth scales, slender body, pale cream ventral scales, dark brown iris, small dark eye, patterned tail, coiled body
08_western_ribbon_snake.wiki_clauses: proximus is blackish, brown, or olive with three light-colored stripes. | The upper labials are whitish and unmarked, contrasting with the dark top and sides of the head.

09_marbled_salamander.visual_traits: bright white dorsal bands, black and silver marbled pattern, dark gray body, pale cream ventral surface, slender body, small dark feet, smooth skin, rounded head, dark brown eyes, black tail, pale cream band along sides
09_marbled_salamander.wiki_clauses: The male is smaller and has white dorsal bands, while the female is larger and has silver dorsal bands. | It exhibits sexual dimorphism with bands of females tending to be light gray, while those of males are bright white.

10_spotted_eagle_ray.visual_traits: white spots on dark blue-black dorsal surface, white underbelly, long slender dark whip-like tail, dark dorsal fins, white pectoral fins, pale cream snout, dark brown eyes, streamlined body, smooth skin
10_spotted_eagle_ray.wiki_clauses: Spotted eagle rays have flat disk-shaped bodies, deep blue or black with white spots on top with a white underbelly, and distinctive flat snouts similar to a duck's bill. | This ray can be identified by its dark dorsal surface covered in white spots or rings.
